bullets: How green plants use light energy to build glucose from carbon dioxide and water, releasing oxygen
slides.heading: Photosynthesis: how plants make food
slides.notes: Welcome everyone in and say: today we follow light energy into a leaf, and by the end you will be able to state the word equation for photosynthesis, name what goes in and what comes out, and explain where the released oxygen really comes from.

bullets: State the word equation for photosynthesis: carbon dioxide + water -> glucose + oxygen, powered by light energy trapped by chlorophyll
Explain where each input comes from, where each product goes, and why plants are called producers
slides.heading: What we will learn
slides.notes: Read the two goals aloud slowly and tell the class: keep these in mind, because our exit ticket at the end will ask you to do exactly these things, including spotting the trap about where the oxygen comes from.

bullets: A seedling gains mass week after week, yet it never eats and the soil in its pot barely loses any mass
The food a plant uses was not taken in ready-made - the plant built it itself
slides.heading: A plant that eats nothing still grows
slides.notes: Show a growing seedling and ask: where did that new mass come from if nothing was eaten? Take two or three answers, then say: hold them, because by the end of the lesson you will be able to trace the food back to air, water and light.

bullets: Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants make glucose using light energy, taking in carbon dioxide and water and releasing oxygen
Chlorophyll, the green pigment in leaves, traps the light energy that powers the change
The word equation is: carbon dioxide + water -> glucose + oxygen
slides.heading: Photosynthesis builds food from air and water
slides.notes: Say this part slowly, because it is the big idea of the whole lesson: the leaf is a food factory, the raw materials are carbon dioxide and water, the energy source is light, and the products are glucose and oxygen.

bullets: Light energy travels from the Sun to the leaf, where photosynthesis happens
Green plants make glucose using light energy: they take in carbon dioxide and water, and release oxygen
slides.heading: Plants make their own food
slides.notes: Point at the animation and narrate what is happening: watch the packets of light energy stream from the Sun into the leaf - that light is the energy input that powers everything that follows.

bullets: Carbon dioxide enters the leaf through tiny pores on its underside
Water is absorbed by the roots and travels up to the leaf
slides.heading: In: carbon dioxide and water
slides.notes: Follow each input as it arrives: carbon dioxide flows in from the air through tiny pores, while water climbs from the roots. Both raw materials must reach the leaf before any food can be built.

bullets: With chlorophyll trapping the light, the plant builds glucose, the food it needs
Oxygen is released from the leaf into the air as a by-product
slides.heading: Out: glucose and oxygen
slides.notes: Watch the products appear: glucose molecules are built inside the leaf and stay as the plant food, while oxygen drifts out into the air. Keep the two products separate in your mind - they have different jobs.

bullets: Light energy powers the change: energy in, food out
Plants are called producers because they make food for almost all life on Earth
slides.heading: Energy in, food out
slides.notes: Trace the energy story: light energy arrives, glucose leaves to feed the plant - and, through food chains, almost every other living thing. That is why plants are called producers.

bullets: Carbon dioxide supplies the carbon for glucose; it is not the source of the released oxygen
Splitting water releases the oxygen, while carbon dioxide goes in and oxygen comes out at different places in the story
slides.heading: Misconception: oxygen does NOT come from CO2
slides.notes: Name the trap out loud before anyone falls into it: the oxygen does not come from the carbon dioxide. Watch the wrong arrow disappear and the right arrow appear - the oxygen comes from water.

bullets: Step 1: inputs are carbon dioxide + water, with light energy trapped by chlorophyll
Step 2: products are glucose + oxygen, so the word equation reads: carbon dioxide + water -> glucose + oxygen
slides.heading: Worked example: the word equation
slides.notes: Talk through the two steps slowly and name each one as you write it; say: notice the energy word sits over the arrow - light energy is the input that makes the building possible.

bullets: Write the word equation for photosynthesis and label the inputs, the products and the energy source
Careful - a classmate claims: The oxygen released in photosynthesis comes from carbon dioxide. Explain to them why that is wrong, and say where the oxygen actually comes from
slides.heading: Your turn: inputs, outputs and the oxygen trap
slides.notes: Give pairs three minutes, then cold-call two pairs for the equation and one pair for the trap: the oxygen comes from water, and carbon dioxide supplies the carbon for glucose.

bullets: On your own: state the word equation and name the inputs and products
Watch out for the trap one last time: The oxygen released in photosynthesis comes from carbon dioxide. Say where the oxygen really comes from
slides.heading: Exit ticket: prove it before you leave
slides.notes: Close by reminding the class of the trap - The oxygen released in photosynthesis comes from carbon dioxide. - and the fix: the released oxygen comes from water. Collect the tickets as they leave and check who still places the oxygen on the carbon dioxide side.
